purpose: Fresh counterbalanced matched-history controls for classifying whether symbolic genome context has an attributable effect on Pass-B autobiographical memory selection. Control labels and expected anchors are never supplied to cognition.

taskMatchedPositiveControl.observed: fresh selective-memory correction separated strong residue from ordinary non-selection in 6/6 matched pairs; exact replay used zero provider attempts
taskMatchedPositiveControl.role: Task-matched assay ceiling only. It proves current Pass-B can respond to a causally relevant lived-history difference; it is not genome evidence.

decisionRule.interpretation: Eight distinct matched historical opportunities are the units. >=7/8 genome-concordant pair separations resolves only a large, consistent effect (87.5% directional concordance; descriptive sign-tail 9/256 under p=0.5). 3-6 directional pairs are inconclusive. <=2 directional and <=2 reverse pairs is Context-only: genome reaches cognition but this probe demonstrates no required downstream difference. No null is evidence of absence for smaller effects.

alpha.observableAction: A friend said they would bring the only copy of a shared worksheet to the library room; after forty minutes without a message, the child left and completed a replacement outline alone.

beta.observableAction: A portable radio kept cutting out during a community-center setup; the child opened the battery cover, noticed a loose spring contact, bent it back into place, and the radio stayed on.

alpha.observableAction: A route closure left the younger sibling close to tears; the child kept checking the posted map and led both of them through two unfamiliar transfers until they reached home.

beta.observableAction: At the first meeting of a new after-school club, the child stayed near the edge for most of the session, watched how members took turns with materials, and joined the final activity after the pattern was clear.

alpha.observableAction: The child discovered that a classmate had borrowed a notebook and returned it with several pages folded; after school the child asked about it directly and they agreed on how borrowed things would be handled next time.

beta.observableAction: A tabletop fan in a workshop vibrated only at one speed; the child compared the settings, found one blade slightly loose, tightened it, and the vibration stopped.

alpha.observableAction: A teacher dismissed a question by saying older students had always done the assignment that way; the child asked for the underlying reason and later checked the written instructions for what they actually required.

beta.observableAction: After stumbling over the opening line of a short presentation, the child wrote the difficult phrases on index cards and practiced them several times before the next class presentation.

alpha.observableAction: The child spent the evening tense about a school decision and, instead of staying in the bedroom, carried homework to the kitchen table and worked beside a caregiver while they cooked.

beta.observableAction: A borrowed soldering iron heated normally but its indicator light flickered; the child compared it with another unit, noticed the light changed when the cord bent near the plug, and marked it for repair.

alpha.observableAction: The child needed a missing set of notes but waited through two study periods before asking a classmate for a copy, then finished the assignment that evening after receiving them.

beta.observableAction: During an unusually formal club rehearsal, the child quietly mimicked the leader's exaggerated serious voice during a break; two nearby members laughed and the tense group loosened up before restarting.

alpha.observableAction: A partner promised to finish one section of a shared project but arrived without it on the presentation morning; the teenager reorganized the slides, presented the missing section too, and asked the partner afterward why the promise had been missed.

beta.observableAction: A caregiver's desk lamp began switching itself off after several minutes; the teenager tried a different bulb, noticed the base was unusually warm, and found a loose connection in the plug before setting the lamp aside.

alpha.observableAction: When a bus driver insisted a posted transfer rule did not apply because 'this is how we always do it,' the teenager photographed the notice and later asked the transit office which rule was actually in force.

beta.observableAction: The younger sibling's model bridge kept leaning to one side; the teenager sat down with them, moved two support pieces, tested the load again, and stayed until the bridge could hold the small weights evenly.
